title: The backups looked fine. They'd been failing for three weeks.
metaDescription: A storage cap, a retention rule that could never fire, and three weeks of green checkmarks over dead backups — what it took to make silence itself an alarm.
tagline: A storage cap, a retention rule that structurally could never fire, and three weeks of green checkmarks over dead backups.
bullets: Every nightly run exited clean — the off-site half hadn't uploaded since June 9
The bucket filled to its storage cap behind a retention rule that could never fire
23 days of green checkmarks over dead backups
Now the script prunes for itself, warnings page a phone, and silence is an alarm

image.label: Timeline — cap exceeded → 23 silent nights → detection → paging

body: The off-site half had failed since June 9, and every run still exited clean — a deliberate choice, so a cloud outage could not block a reboot. Reasonable, plus nobody reading warnings, equals three weeks of green.

sections.h: The fix was mostly not code
body: The retention rule looked right — keep seven days, delete the rest — but it only removes prior versions of overwritten files, and every bundle was a unique name. Perfectly configured to do nothing, forever.
Exit codes are claims, not facts. A monthly restore drill is on the calendar now, because a backup you have never restored is a hypothesis, not a backup.
